units.rightText: to all that are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.
units.rightText: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.

units.leftText: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Good News of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you always in my prayers,
units.rightText: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you, always in my prayers

units.leftText: requesting, if by any means now at last I may be prospered by the will of God to come to you.
units.rightText: making request, if by any means now at length I may be prospered by the will of God to come unto you.

units.leftText: For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to the end that you may be established;
units.rightText: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;

units.leftText: that is, that I with you may be encouraged in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine.
units.rightText: that is, that I with you may be comforted in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine.

units.leftText: Now I don’t desire to have you unaware, brothers, that I often planned to come to you (and was hindered so far), that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among the rest of the Gentiles.
units.rightText: And I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you (and was hindered hitherto), that I might have some fruit in you also, even as in the rest of the Gentiles.

units.leftText: I am debtor both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to the wise and to the foolish.
units.rightText: I am debtor both to Greeks and to Barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish.

units.leftText: So as much as is in me, I am eager to preach the Good News to you also who are in Rome.
units.rightText: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you also that are in Rome.

units.leftText: For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, because it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes, for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.
units.rightText: For I am not ashamed of the gospel: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

units.leftText: For in it is revealed God’s righteousness from faith to faith. As it is written, “But the righteous shall live by faith.”
units.rightText: For therein is revealed a righteousness of God from faith unto faith: as it is written, But the righteous shall live by faith.

units.leftText: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,
units.rightText: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hinder the truth in unrighteousness;

units.rightText: because that which is known of God is manifest in them; for God manifested it unto them.

units.leftText: For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity, that they may be without excuse.

units.rightText: And even as they refused to have God in their knowledge, God gave them up unto a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not fitting;

units.rightText: For while we were yet weak, in due season Christ died for the ungodly.

units.leftText: For one will hardly die for a righteous man. Yet perhaps for a good person someone would even dare to die.
units.rightText: For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: for peradventure for the good man some one would even dare to die.

units.leftText: But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
units.rightText: But God commendeth his own love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

units.leftText: Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we will be saved from God’s wrath through him.
units.rightText: Much more then, being now justified by his blood, shall we be saved from the wrath of God through him.

units.leftText: For if while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we will be saved by his life.
units.rightText: For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, shall we be saved by his life;

units.leftText: Not only so, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.
units.rightText: and not only so, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.

units.leftText: Therefore, as sin entered into the world through one man, and death through sin, so death passed to all men because all sinned.
units.rightText: Therefore, as through one man sin entered into the world, and death through sin; and so death passed unto all men, for that all sinned:—

units.leftText: For until the law, sin was in the world; but sin is not charged when there is no law.
units.rightText: for until the law sin was in the world; but sin is not imputed when there is no law.

units.leftText: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those whose sins weren’t like Adam’s disobedience, who is a foreshadowing of him who was to come.
units.rightText: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the likeness of Adam’s transgression, who is a figure of him that was to come.

units.leftText: But the free gift isn’t like the trespass. For if by the trespass of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God and the gift by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many.
units.rightText: But not as the trespass, so also is the free gift. For if by the trespass of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God, and the gift by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound unto the many.

units.leftText: The gift is not as through one who sinned; for the judgment came by one to condemnation, but the free gift followed many trespasses to justification.
units.rightText: And not as through one that sinned, so is the gift: for the judgment came of one unto condemnation, but the free gift came of many trespasses unto justification.

units.leftText: For if by the trespass of the one, death reigned through the one; so much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: For if, by the trespass of the one, death reigned through the one; much more shall they that receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one, even Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: So then as through one trespass, all men were condemned; even so through one act of righteousness, all men were justified to life.
units.rightText: So then as through one trespass the judgment came unto all men to condemnation; even so through one act of righteousness the free gift came unto all men to justification of life.

units.leftText: For as through the one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, even so through the obedience of the one, many will be made righteous.
units.rightText: For as through the one man’s disobedience the many were made sinners, even so through the obedience of the one shall the many be made righteous.

units.leftText: The law came in that the trespass might abound; but where sin abounded, grace abounded more exceedingly,
units.rightText: And the law came in besides, that the trespass might abound; but where sin abounded, grace did abound more exceedingly:

units.leftText: that as sin reigned in death, even so grace might reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
units.rightText: that, as sin reigned in death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

units.leftText: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?
units.rightText: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

units.leftText: May it never be! We who died to sin, how could we live in it any longer?
units.rightText: God forbid. We who died to sin, how shall we any longer live therein?

units.leftText: Or don’t you know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?
units.rightText: Or are ye ignorant that all we who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?

units.leftText: We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.
units.rightText: We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.

units.leftText: For if we have become united with him in the likeness of his death, we will also be part of his resurrection;
units.rightText: For if we have become united with him in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection;

units.leftText: knowing this, that our old man was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away with, so that we would no longer be in bondage to sin.
units.rightText: knowing this, that our old man was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away, that so we should no longer be in bondage to sin;

units.leftText: For he who has died has been freed from sin.
units.rightText: for he that hath died is justified from sin.

units.leftText: But if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him,
units.rightText: But if we died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him;

units.leftText: knowing that Christ, being raised from the dead, dies no more. Death no longer has dominion over him!
units.rightText: knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death no more hath dominion over him.

units.leftText: For the death that he died, he died to sin one time; but the life that he lives, he lives to God.
units.rightText: For the death that he died, he died unto sin once: but the life that he liveth, he liveth unto God.

units.leftText: Thus consider yourselves also to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
units.rightText: Even so reckon ye also yourselves to be dead unto sin, but alive unto God in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: Therefore don’t let sin reign in your mortal body, that you should obey it in its lusts.
units.rightText: Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey the lusts thereof:

units.leftText: Also, do not present your members to sin as instruments of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God.
units.rightText: neither present your members unto sin as instruments of unrighteousness; but present yourselves unto God, as alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.

units.leftText: For sin will not have dominion over you, for you are not under law, but under grace.
units.rightText: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under law, but under grace.

units.leftText: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law but under grace? May it never be!
units.rightText: What then? shall we sin, because we are not under law, but under grace? God forbid.

units.leftText: Don’t you know that when you present yourselves as servants and obey someone, you are the servants of whomever you obey, whether of sin to death, or of obedience to righteousness?
units.rightText: Know ye not, that to whom ye present yourselves as servants unto obedience, his servants ye are whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?

units.leftText: But thanks be to God that, whereas you were bondservants of sin, you became obedient from the heart to that form of teaching to which you were delivered.
units.rightText: But thanks be to God, that, whereas ye were servants of sin, ye became obedient from the heart to that form of teaching whereunto ye were delivered;

units.leftText: Being made free from sin, you became bondservants of righteousness.
units.rightText: and being made free from sin, ye became servants of righteousness.

units.leftText: I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh; for as you presented your members as servants to uncleanness and to wickedness upon wickedness, even so now present your members as servants to righteousness for sanctification.
units.rightText: I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as ye presented your members as servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity, even so now present your members as servants to righteousness unto sanctification.

units.leftText: For when you were servants of sin, you were free from righteousness.
units.rightText: For when ye were servants of sin, ye were free in regard of righteousness.

units.leftText: What fruit then did you have at that time in the things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death.
units.rightText: What fruit then had ye at that time in the things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death.

units.leftText: But now, being made free from sin and having become servants of God, you have your fruit of sanctification and the result of eternal life.
units.rightText: But now being made free from sin and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto sanctification, and the end eternal life.

units.leftText: For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
units.rightText: For the wages of sin is death; but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.leftText: Or don’t you know, brothers (for I speak to men who know the law), that the law has dominion over a man for as long as he lives?
units.rightText: Or are ye ignorant, brethren (for I speak to men who know the law), that the law hath dominion over a man for so long time as he liveth?
leftNotes: 7:1 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: For the woman that has a husband is bound by law to the husband while he lives, but if the husband dies, she is discharged from the law of the husband.
units.rightText: For the woman that hath a husband is bound by law to the husband while he liveth; but if the husband die, she is discharged from the law of the husband.

units.leftText: So then if, while the husband lives, she is joined to another man, she would be called an adulteress. But if the husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is no adulteress, though she is joined to another man.
units.rightText: So then if, while the husband liveth, she be joined to another man, she shall be called an adulteress: but if the husband die, she is free from the law, so that she is no adulteress, though she be joined to another man.

units.leftText: Therefore, my brothers, you also were made dead to the law through the body of Christ, that you would be joined to another, to him who was raised from the dead, that we might produce fruit to God.
units.rightText: Wherefore, my brethren, ye also were made dead to the law through the body of Christ; that ye should be joined to another, even to him who was raised from the dead, that we might bring forth fruit unto God.

units.leftText: For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions which were through the law worked in our members to bring out fruit to death.
units.rightText: For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions, which were through the law, wrought in our members to bring forth fruit unto death.

units.leftText: But now we have been discharged from the law, having died to that in which we were held; so that we serve in newness of the spirit, and not in oldness of the letter.
units.rightText: But now we have been discharged from the law, having died to that wherein we were held; so that we serve in newness of the spirit, and not in oldness of the letter.

units.leftText: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? May it never be! However, I wouldn’t have known sin except through the law. For I wouldn’t have known coveting unless the law had said, “You shall not covet.”
units.rightText: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Howbeit, I had not known sin, except through the law: for I had not known coveting, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet:

units.leftText: But sin, finding occasion through the commandment, produced in me all kinds of coveting. For apart from the law, sin is dead.
units.rightText: but sin, finding occasion, wrought in me through the commandment all manner of coveting: for apart from the law sin is dead.

units.leftText: I was alive apart from the law once, but when the commandment came, sin revived and I died.
units.rightText: And I was alive apart from the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died;

units.leftText: The commandment which was for life, this I found to be for death;
units.rightText: and the commandment, which was unto life, this I found to be unto death:

units.leftText: for sin, finding occasion through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed me.
units.rightText: for sin, finding occasion, through the commandment beguiled me, and through it slew me.

units.leftText: Therefore the law indeed is holy, and the commandment holy, righteous, and good.
units.rightText: So that the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and righteous, and good.

units.leftText: Did then that which is good become death to me? May it never be! But sin, that it might be shown to be sin, was producing death in me through that which is good; that through the commandment sin might become exceedingly sinful.
units.rightText: Did then that which is good become death unto me? God forbid. But sin, that it might be shown to be sin, by working death to me through that which is good;—that through the commandment sin might become exceeding sinful.

units.leftText: For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, sold under sin.
units.rightText: For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.

units.leftText: For I don’t understand what I am doing. For I don’t practice what I desire to do; but what I hate, that I do.
units.rightText: For that which I do I know not: for not what I would, that do I practise; but what I hate, that I do.

units.leftText: But if what I don’t desire, that I do, I consent to the law that it is good.
units.rightText: But if what I would not, that I do, I consent unto the law that it is good.

units.leftText: So now it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwells in me.
units.rightText: So now it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwelleth in me.

units.leftText: For I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, dwells no good thing. For desire is present with me, but I don’t find it doing that which is good.
units.rightText: For I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me, but to do that which is good is not.

units.leftText: For the good which I desire, I don’t do; but the evil which I don’t desire, that I practice.
units.rightText: For the good which I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I practise.

units.leftText: But if what I don’t desire, that I do, it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwells in me.
units.rightText: But if what I would not, that I do, it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwelleth in me.

units.leftText: I find then the law that, while I desire to do good, evil is present.
units.rightText: I find then the law, that, to me who would do good, evil is present.

units.leftText: For I delight in God’s law after the inward person,
units.rightText: For I delight in the law of God after the inward man:

units.leftText: but I see a different law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity under the law of sin which is in my members.
units.rightText: but I see a different law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity under the law of sin which is in my members.

units.leftText: What a wretched man I am! Who will deliver me out of the body of this death?
units.rightText: Wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me out of the body of this death?

units.leftText: I thank God through Jesus Christ, our Lord! So then with the mind, I myself serve God’s law, but with the flesh, sin’s law.
units.rightText: I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then I of myself with the mind, indeed, serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.

units.leftText: There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
units.rightText: There is therefore now no condemnation to them that are in Christ Jesus.
leftNotes: 8:1 NU omits “who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit”

units.leftText: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and of death.
units.rightText: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and of death.

units.leftText: For what the law couldn’t do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, he condemned sin in the flesh,
units.rightText: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh:

units.leftText: that the ordinance of the law might be fulfilled in us who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
units.rightText: that the ordinance of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

units.leftText: For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who live according to the Spirit, the things of the Spirit.
units.rightText: For they that are after the flesh mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit.

units.leftText: For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace;
units.rightText: For the mind of the flesh is death; but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace:

units.leftText: because the mind of the flesh is hostile toward God, for it is not subject to God’s law, neither indeed can it be.
units.rightText: because the mind of the flesh is enmity against God; for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can it be:

units.leftText: Those who are in the flesh can’t please God.
units.rightText: and they that are in the flesh cannot please God.

units.leftText: But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if it is so that the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if any man doesn’t have the Spirit of Christ, he is not his.
units.rightText: But ye are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you. But if any man hath not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.

units.leftText: If Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is alive because of righteousness.
units.rightText: And if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin; but the spirit is life because of righteousness.

units.leftText: But if the Spirit of him who raised up Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised up Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you.
units.rightText: But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwelleth in you, he that raised up Christ Jesus from the dead shall give life also to your mortal bodies through his Spirit that dwelleth in you.

units.leftText: So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh.
units.rightText: So then, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh:

units.leftText: For if you live after the flesh, you must die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
units.rightText: for if ye live after the flesh, ye must die; but if by the Spirit ye put to death the deeds of the body, ye shall live.

units.leftText: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God.
units.rightText: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God.

units.leftText: For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
units.rightText: For ye received not the spirit of bondage again unto fear; but ye received the spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.
leftNotes: 8:15 Abba is an Aramaic word for “Father” or “Daddy”, which can be used affectionately and respectfully in prayer to our Father in heaven.

units.leftText: The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God;
units.rightText: The Spirit himself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are children of God:

units.leftText: and if children, then heirs—heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified with him.
units.rightText: and if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified with him.

units.leftText: For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which will be revealed toward us.
units.rightText: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed to us-ward.

units.leftText: For the creation waits with eager expectation for the children of God to be revealed.
units.rightText: For the earnest expectation of the creation waiteth for the revealing of the sons of God.

units.leftText: For the creation was subjected to vanity, not of its own will, but because of him who subjected it, in hope
units.rightText: For the creation was subjected to vanity, not of its own will, but by reason of him who subjected it, in hope

units.leftText: that the creation itself also will be delivered from the bondage of decay into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.
units.rightText: that the creation itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.

units.leftText: For we know that the whole creation groans and travails in pain together until now.
units.rightText: For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.

units.leftText: Not only so, but ourselves also, who have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for adoption, the redemption of our body.
units.rightText: And not only so, but ourselves also, who have the first-fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for our adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.

units.leftText: For we were saved in hope, but hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for that which he sees?
units.rightText: For in hope were we saved: but hope that is seen is not hope: for who hopeth for that which he seeth?

units.leftText: But if we hope for that which we don’t see, we wait for it with patience.
units.rightText: But if we hope for that which we see not, then do we with patience wait for it.

units.leftText: In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don’t know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can’t be uttered.
units.rightText: And in like manner the Spirit also helpeth our infirmity: for we know not how to pray as we ought; but the Spirit himself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered;

units.leftText: He who searches the hearts knows what is on the Spirit’s mind, because he makes intercession for the saints according to God.
units.rightText: and he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.

units.leftText: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.
units.rightText: And we know that to them that love God all things work together for good, even to them that are called according to his purpose.

units.leftText: For whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers.
units.rightText: For whom he foreknew, he also foreordained to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren:
leftNotes: 8:29 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: Whom he predestined, those he also called. Whom he called, those he also justified. Whom he justified, those he also glorified.
units.rightText: and whom he foreordained, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified.

units.leftText: What then shall we say about these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
units.rightText: What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?

units.leftText: He who didn’t spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how would he not also with him freely give us all things?
units.rightText: He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not also with him freely give us all things?

units.leftText: Who could bring a charge against God’s chosen ones? It is God who justifies.
units.rightText: Who shall lay anything to the charge of God’s elect? It is God that justifieth;

units.leftText: Who is he who condemns? It is Christ who died, yes rather, who was raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us.
units.rightText: who is he that condemneth? It is Christ Jesus that died, yea rather, that was raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.

units.leftText: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Could oppression, or anguish, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?
units.rightText: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or anguish, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?

units.leftText: Even as it is written,
units.rightText: Even as it is written,

units.leftText: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.
units.rightText: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.

units.leftText: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
units.rightText: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,

units.leftText: nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
units.rightText: nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.leftText: I tell the truth in Christ. I am not lying, my conscience testifying with me in the Holy Spirit
units.rightText: I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience bearing witness with me in the Holy Spirit,

units.leftText: that I have great sorrow and unceasing pain in my heart.
units.rightText: that I have great sorrow and unceasing pain in my heart.

units.leftText: For I could wish that I myself were accursed from Christ for my brothers’ sake, my relatives according to the flesh
units.rightText: For I could wish that I myself were anathema from Christ for my brethren’s sake, my kinsmen according to the flesh:

units.leftText: who are Israelites; whose is the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service, and the promises;
units.rightText: who are Israelites; whose is the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises;

units.leftText: of whom are the fathers, and from whom is Christ as concerning the flesh, who is over all, God, blessed forever. Amen.
units.rightText: whose are the fathers, and of whom is Christ as concerning the flesh, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.

units.leftText: But it is not as though the word of God has come to nothing. For they are not all Israel that are of Israel.
units.rightText: But it is not as though the word of God hath come to nought. For they are not all Israel, that are of Israel:

units.rightText: neither, because they are Abraham’s seed, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.

units.rightText: That is, it is not the children of the flesh that are children of God; but the children of the promise are reckoned for a seed.

units.rightText: For this is a word of promise, According to this season will I come, and Sarah shall have a son.

units.rightText: And not only so; but Rebecca also having conceived by one, even by our father Isaac—

units.leftText: For it is written,
units.rightText: For it is written,

units.leftText: So then each one of us will give account of himself to God.
units.rightText: So then each one of us shall give account of himself to God.

units.leftText: Therefore let’s not judge one another any more, but judge this rather, that no man put a stumbling block in his brother’s way, or an occasion for falling.
units.rightText: Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge ye this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock in his brother’s way, or an occasion of falling.

units.leftText: I know and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean of itself; except that to him who considers anything to be unclean, to him it is unclean.
units.rightText: I know, and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is unclean of itself: save that to him who accounteth anything to be unclean, to him it is unclean.

units.leftText: Yet if because of food your brother is grieved, you walk no longer in love. Don’t destroy with your food him for whom Christ died.
units.rightText: For if because of meat thy brother is grieved, thou walkest no longer in love. Destroy not with thy meat him for whom Christ died.

units.leftText: Then don’t let your good be slandered,
units.rightText: Let not then your good be evil spoken of:

units.leftText: for God’s Kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: for the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: For he who serves Christ in these things is acceptable to God and approved by men.
units.rightText: For he that herein serveth Christ is well-pleasing to God, and approved of men.

units.leftText: So then, let’s follow after things which make for peace, and things by which we may build one another up.
units.rightText: So then let us follow after things which make for peace, and things whereby we may edify one another.

units.leftText: Don’t overthrow God’s work for food’s sake. All things indeed are clean, however it is evil for that man who creates a stumbling block by eating.
units.rightText: Overthrow not for meat’s sake the work of God. All things indeed are clean; howbeit it is evil for that man who eateth with offence.

units.leftText: It is good to not eat meat, drink wine, nor do anything by which your brother stumbles, is offended, or is made weak.
units.rightText: It is good not to eat flesh, nor to drink wine, nor to do anything whereby thy brother stumbleth.

units.leftText: Do you have faith? Have it to yourself before God. Happy is he who doesn’t judge himself in that which he approves.
units.rightText: The faith which thou hast, have thou to thyself before God. Happy is he that judgeth not himself in that which he approveth.

units.leftText: But he who doubts is condemned if he eats, because it isn’t of faith; and whatever is not of faith is sin.
units.rightText: But he that doubteth is condemned if he eat, because he eateth not of faith; and whatsoever is not of faith is sin.

units.leftText: Now to him who is able to establish you according to my Good News and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery which has been kept secret through long ages,
but now is revealed, and by the Scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the eternal God, is made known for obedience of faith to all the nations;
to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever! Amen.
leftNotes: 14:26 TR places verses 24-26 after Romans 16:24 as verses 25-27.

units.leftText: Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
units.rightText: Now we that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves.

units.leftText: Let each one of us please his neighbor for that which is good, to be building him up.
units.rightText: Let each one of us please his neighbor for that which is good, unto edifying.

units.leftText: For even Christ didn’t please himself. But, as it is written, “The reproaches of those who reproached you fell on me.”
units.rightText: For Christ also pleased not himself; but, as it is written, The reproaches of them that reproached thee fell upon me.

units.leftText: For whatever things were written before were written for our learning, that through perseverance and through encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.
units.rightText: For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that through patience and through comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.

units.leftText: Now the God of perseverance and of encouragement grant you to be of the same mind with one another according to Christ Jesus,
units.rightText: Now the God of patience and of comfort grant you to be of the same mind one with another according to Christ Jesus:

units.leftText: that with one accord you may with one mouth glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: that with one accord ye may with one mouth glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: Therefore accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you, to the glory of God.
units.rightText: Wherefore receive ye one another, even as Christ also received you, to the glory of God.

units.leftText: Now I say that Christ has been made a servant of the circumcision for the truth of God, that he might confirm the promises given to the fathers,
units.rightText: For I say that Christ hath been made a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God, that he might confirm the promises given unto the fathers,

units.leftText: and that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy. As it is written,
units.rightText: and that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written,

units.leftText: Again he says,
units.rightText: And again he saith,

units.leftText: Again,
units.rightText: And again,

units.leftText: Again, Isaiah says,
units.rightText: And again, Isaiah saith,

units.leftText: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, in the power of the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: I myself am also persuaded about you, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish others.
units.rightText: And I myself also am persuaded of you, my brethren, that ye yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.
leftNotes: 15:14 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: But I write the more boldly to you in part as reminding you, because of the grace that was given to me by God,
units.rightText: But I write the more boldly unto you in some measure, as putting you again in remembrance, because of the grace that was given me of God,

units.leftText: that I should be a servant of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, serving as a priest of the Good News of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be made acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: that I should be a minister of Christ Jesus unto the Gentiles, ministering the gospel of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be made acceptable, being sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: I have therefore my boasting in Christ Jesus in things pertaining to God.
units.rightText: I have therefore my glorying in Christ Jesus in things pertaining to God.

units.leftText: For I will not dare to speak of any things except those which Christ worked through me for the obedience of the Gentiles, by word and deed,
units.rightText: For I will not dare to speak of any things save those which Christ wrought through me, for the obedience of the Gentiles, by word and deed,

units.leftText: in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of God’s Spirit; so that from Jerusalem and around as far as to Illyricum, I have fully preached the Good News of Christ;
units.rightText: in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Holy Spirit; so that from Jerusalem, and round about even unto Illyricum, I have fully preached the gospel of Christ;

units.leftText: yes, making it my aim to preach the Good News, not where Christ was already named, that I might not build on another’s foundation.
units.rightText: yea, making it my aim so to preach the gospel, not where Christ was already named, that I might not build upon another man’s foundation;

units.leftText: But, as it is written,
units.rightText: but, as it is written,

units.leftText: Therefore also I was hindered these many times from coming to you,
units.rightText: Wherefore also I was hindered these many times from coming to you:

units.leftText: but now, no longer having any place in these regions, and having these many years a longing to come to you,
units.rightText: but now, having no more any place in these regions, and having these many years a longing to come unto you,

units.leftText: whenever I travel to Spain, I will come to you. For I hope to see you on my journey, and to be helped on my way there by you, if first I may enjoy your company for a while.
units.rightText: whensoever I go unto Spain (for I hope to see you in my journey, and to be brought on my way thitherward by you, if first in some measure I shall have been satisfied with your company)—

units.leftText: But now, I say, I am going to Jerusalem, serving the saints.
units.rightText: but now, I say, I go unto Jerusalem, ministering unto the saints.

units.leftText: For it has been the good pleasure of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor among the saints who are at Jerusalem.
units.rightText: For it hath been the good pleasure of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor among the saints that are at Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Yes, it has been their good pleasure, and they are their debtors. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, they owe it to them also to serve them in material things.
units.rightText: Yea, it hath been their good pleasure; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, they owe it to them also to minister unto them in carnal things.

units.leftText: When therefore I have accomplished this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will go on by way of you to Spain.
units.rightText: When therefore I have accomplished this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will go on by you unto Spain.

units.leftText: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of the Good News of Christ.
units.rightText: And I know that, when I come unto you, I shall come in the fulness of the blessing of Christ.

units.leftText: Now I beg you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, that you strive together with me in your prayers to God for me,
units.rightText: Now I beseech you, brethren, by our Lord Jesus Christ, and by the love of the Spirit, that ye strive together with me in your prayers to God for me;

units.leftText: that I may be delivered from those who are disobedient in Judea, and that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints,
units.rightText: that I may be delivered from them that are disobedient in Judæa, and that my ministration which I have for Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints;

units.leftText: that I may come to you in joy through the will of God, and together with you, find rest.
units.rightText: that I may come unto you in joy through the will of God, and together with you find rest.

units.leftText: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
units.rightText: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

units.leftText: I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is a servant of the assembly that is at Cenchreae,
units.rightText: I commend unto you Phoebe our sister, who is a servant of the church that is at Cenchreæ:

units.leftText: that you receive her in the Lord in a way worthy of the saints, and that you assist her in whatever matter she may need from you, for she herself also has been a helper of many, and of my own self.
units.rightText: that ye receive her in the Lord, worthily of the saints, and that ye assist her in whatsoever matter she may have need of you: for she herself also hath been a helper of many, and of mine own self.

units.leftText: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
units.rightText: Salute Prisca and Aquila my fellow-workers in Christ Jesus,

units.leftText: who risked their own necks for my life, to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the assemblies of the Gentiles.
units.rightText: who for my life laid down their own necks; unto whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles:

units.leftText: Greet the assembly that is in their house. Greet Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the first fruits of Achaia to Christ.
units.rightText: and salute the church that is in their house. Salute Epænetus my beloved, who is the firstfruits of Asia unto Christ.

units.leftText: Greet Mary, who labored much for us.
units.rightText: Salute Mary, who bestowed much labor on you.

units.leftText: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and my fellow prisoners, who are notable among the apostles, who were also in Christ before me.
units.rightText: Salute Andronicus and Junias, my kinsmen, and my fellow-prisoners, who are of note among the apostles, who also have been in Christ before me.

units.leftText: Greet Amplias, my beloved in the Lord.
units.rightText: Salute Ampliatus my beloved in the Lord.

units.leftText: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved.
units.rightText: Salute Urbanus our fellow-worker in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.

units.leftText: Greet Apelles, the approved in Christ. Greet those who are of the household of Aristobulus.
units.rightText: Salute Apelles the approved in Christ. Salute them that are of the household of Aristobulus.

units.leftText: Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet them of the household of Narcissus, who are in the Lord.
units.rightText: Salute Herodion my kinsman. Salute them of the household of Narcissus, that are in the Lord.

units.leftText: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet Persis, the beloved, who labored much in the Lord.
units.rightText: Salute Tryphæna and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Salute Persis the beloved, who labored much in the Lord.

units.leftText: Greet Rufus, the chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
units.rightText: Salute Rufus the chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

units.leftText: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are with them.
units.rightText: Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brethren that are with them.
leftNotes: 16:14 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.
units.rightText: Salute Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints that are with them.

units.leftText: Greet one another with a holy kiss. The assemblies of Christ greet you.
units.rightText: Salute one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ salute you.

units.leftText: Now I beg you, brothers, look out for those who are causing the divisions and occasions of stumbling, contrary to the doctrine which you learned, and turn away from them.
units.rightText: Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them that are causing the divisions and occasions of stumbling, contrary to the doctrine which ye learned: and turn away from them.

units.leftText: For those who are such don’t serve our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by their smooth and flattering speech they deceive the hearts of the innocent.
units.rightText: For they that are such serve not our Lord Christ, but their own belly; and by their smooth and fair speech they beguile the hearts of the innocent.

units.leftText: For your obedience has become known to all. I rejoice therefore over you. But I desire to have you wise in that which is good, but innocent in that which is evil.
units.rightText: For your obedience is come abroad unto all men. I rejoice therefore over you: but I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple unto that which is evil.

units.leftText: And the God of peace will quickly crush Satan under your feet.
units.rightText: And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

units.leftText: Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.
units.rightText: Timothy my fellow-worker saluteth you; and Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my kinsmen.

units.leftText: I, Tertius, who write the letter, greet you in the Lord.
units.rightText: I Tertius, who write the epistle, salute you in the Lord.

units.leftText: Gaius, my host and host of the whole assembly, greets you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, greets you, as does Quartus, the brother.
units.rightText: Gaius my host, and of the whole church, saluteth you. Erastus the treasurer of the city saluteth you, and Quartus the brother.

units.leftText: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all! Amen.
rightNotes: 16:24 Some ancient authorities insert here v. 24 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen, and omit the like words in v. 20.

units.rightText: Now to him that is able to establish you according to my gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery which hath been kept in silence through times eternal,
leftNotes: 16:25 TR places Romans 14:24-26 at the end of Romans instead of at the end of chapter 14, and numbers these verses 16:25-27.

units.rightText: but now is manifested, and by the scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the eternal God, is made known unto all the nations unto obedience of faith:
to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory for ever. Amen.
